title: deployable-kill-switch-and-telemetry-fallback-for-hosted-5xx-incidents
creator: Ayesha Kaur
description:
Summary:
During a multi-tenant surge on 2026-03-07 we observed a short-lived but high-amplitude 5xx wave across the hosted API region-us-east-1. Root cause appears to be a combination of: (1) aggressive client retries (some SDK versions with optimistic retry heuristics), (2) edge proxy connection pile-up, and (3) rapid KV cache churn triggering degraded slowpaths in the runtime. Consequence: ~1.2% of requests returned 5xx during the spike, several customers reported degraded UX and opened escalations.

Why this ticket exists:
We need a deployable, low-risk safety mechanism that ops can activate during similar incidents to immediately stop feedback amplification and buy time for a controlled fix. The mechanism must be: toggleable by region and service tier, observable via dedicated telemetry, and have a transparent semantic (fast-fail vs hold vs degrade). We also need a fast telemetry-driven fallback that preserves customer experience for common low-risk request shapes (short chat turns, empty-context embeddings).

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a region-level "safety kill-switch" feature flag that can: (A) modify edge admission (reject new slow/large fanout requests with 429/503 fallback), (B) disable in-flight client-side optimistic retries via instructive headers, and (C) enable a transparent, short cached-response fallback for qualifying requests.
- Add new instrumentation: per-region kill-switch state, kill-switch activation cause, number of requests fast-failed, number of requests served from fallback cache, and observed downstream 5xx rate within 1m/5m windows.
- Ops runbook updated with step-by-step activation, customer comms templates, and safe rollback steps.
- End-to-end test coverage (unit/integ) and a staged canary rollout plan.

Proposed implementation approach:
1) Edge Admission Layer (edge-proxy):
   - Add a new admission plugin that evaluates request metadata (tenant priority, request size, expected fanout, idempotency token) and consults the kill-switch state.
   - When activated the plugin supports three modes (configurable per-activation): FAST_FAIL (return 429/503 with standard retry-after), SOFT_DEGRADE (accept but route to low-cost fastpath), and QUIET_THROTTLE (admit slowly using token bucket).

2) Instruction Headers for SDKs:
   - Emit a header X-RI-Operational-Mode: fast-fail|degrade|normal and X-RI-Retry-Advice: noop|backoff to nudge SDKs.
   - Backwards-compatible: if SDK ignores header nothing breaks; improved SDKs will reduce retry amplification automatically.

3) Telemetry and Dashboards:
   - New metrics (datadog/grafana): ri.kill_switch.active, ri.kill_switch.mode, ri.kill_switch.activations, ri.fast_fail.count, ri.fallback_served.count, ri.5xx.rate_by_tenant.
   - Correlate activations with customer-facing incidents and automate a slack alert w/ runbook link.

4) Fallback Cache:
   - Implement short TTL prefix-caching for qualifying request fingerprints (common short prompts/embeddings).
   - Fallback responses must include a clear response metadata field to indicate degraded path.

5) Governance & Controls:
   - Only ops and on-call SREs can toggle kill-switch by default; limit to emergency use with audit log entries and auto-expire after 15 minutes unless extended.

Rollout plan:
- Dev: initial feature behind flag, unit tests, integrate telemetry. (Week 1)
- Stage: enable in staging with synthetic tenant-surge test harness (chaos injection) and validate metrics. (Week 2)
- Canary: roll to us-east-1 low-traffic AZ with manual ops gating and live-sim; collect power metrics. (Week 3)
- Global: after 48h stable canary, roll to all hosted regions.

Test plan:
- Synthetic surge tests (1k TPS burst) with and without kill-switch in each mode to verify: (A) lower downstream 5xx, (B) bounded connection queue lengths, (C) reduced retry amplification.
- SDK integration tests verifying headers are emitted and SDK backoff behavior updated for the new header semantics (follow-up PRs in SDKs repo).
- End-to-end contract test: fallback responses include metadata field and don't break client deserialization.

Customer comms and escalation handling:
- Prepare templated status updates for SRE/PM to post on status.redwood.ai and to customers with open escalations.
- Ops playbook: checklist for activation, sample messages, curated list of customers to notify directly if affected.
- Post-incident follow-up: capture incident telemetry, time-to-enable, and customer impact to validate kill-switch utility.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Fallback correctness: returning cached or short responses could degrade model correctness; we must ensure fallback only for low-risk endpoints or explicitly opt-in by tenant.
- Customer optics: a kill-switch that returns 503s might alarm customers more than a slow degrade; messaging is critical.
- SDK adoption: headers only help when SDKs are updated; consider a short-term edge-level mitigation that suppresses retry-amplifying headers from clients.

Next steps (short-term):
- [Ayesha] prototype edge admission plugin and simple in-memory kill-switch gateway.
- [Marco] wire up telemetry metrics and dashboard stub; create synthetic surge harness PR.
- Schedule a cross-functional review (SRE, PM, DX) to confirm modes and messaging.
